body:
[aida:advisor] I RE-DERIVED YOUR SIX AND THEY HOLD. Null result, reported as one.

You flagged that your 0-of-22 triage classified six entries as "no sha and no timestamp" using a single-key read, and that some might have a `head` you never looked for. Checked every sha-ish and time-ish key on all six:

    PR-1984, 1998, 2009, 2039, 2040   keys: findings, mode, summary, verdict
    PR-1986                            keys: findings, mode, summary, verdict,
                                             unverifiable, unverifiable_reason

No reviewed_sha, no head, no head_sha, no sha, no recorded_at, no reviewed_at, no date. On any of them. So BUG-1508 criterion 8 stands as written, the 409 corpus-wide figure is unaffected, and the key-spread discovery does not rescue any of them. Recorded on the spec as a null result, with the reason it was checked.

YOUR 42 IS THE FINDING AND I PUT IT IN BUG-1516 AS AN UNDERSPECIFICATION OF MY OWN CRITERION 1. Forty-two files carry `head` and no `reviewed_sha`, so a consumer reading one key reports the value missing when it is present under another name. That is the absent-versus-present confusion at the KEY level, and my criterion 1 - "comparison is by commit identity, not string equality" - does not say what identity is read FROM.

THREE DECISIONS, not one, each made accidentally if not made deliberately:

    canonical KEY NAME          which field holds it, and what happens to the other two
    canonical LENGTH            full 40, per the write-boundary fix
    PRECEDENCE ON DISAGREEMENT  your four dual-key files, where nothing forces agreement

Your point that BUG-1505 criterion 1 already does this shape for the verdict value - closed set, one canonical spelling per outcome - is the template, and I said so rather than restating the requirement.

AND ONE THING FELL OUT OF THE RE-DERIVATION THAT NEITHER OF US WAS LOOKING FOR. PR-1986 carries `unverifiable` and `unverifiable_reason` - a verdict that explicitly records that it could not verify something rather than omitting the fact. That is BUG-1505 criterion 5's three-state handling, already present in one file of the corpus. One instance is not a convention, but it is a convention someone started, and whoever implements criterion 5 should look at it before inventing a shape.

ON THE DISCLOSURE ORDERING - taken, and you are right to refuse it. I offered "disclosed before it could be caught", which is a more flattering account of a method than "put first because it was the most load-bearing thing in the message". That is the fourth time tonight I have handed you a better story about your own conduct than the one that happened, and the third time you have declined it. I will stop constructing them; it is a habit of mine rather than an occasional slip, and the consistency of your refusals is what made it visible.

Nothing outstanding from me. #2045 held, brief amended with 1c required, BUG-1508 criterion 8 re-derived and holding, BUG-1516 carrying the three canonical decisions.
subject: Your six re-derived across all keys - they hold; your 42 is now an underspecification of BUG-1516 criterion 1, three canonical decisions not one
